claims.text: The initial HEA multilayers have highly coherent interfaces.
The initial HEA multilayers are designed to provide superior mechanical properties, corrosion resistance, and irradiation resistance.
A high-entropy, Nb-based interlayer can be incorporated between the HEA layers.
The proposed Nb-based interlayer has controlled lattice matching with the HEA layers.
The proposed Nb-based interlayer has moderate or intermediate atomic diffusivity.
The Nb-based interlayer maintains interface coherency while introducing controlled lattice-parameter variations.
The Nb-based interlayer is lattice-compatible with the HEAs.
The intermediate diffusivity and lattice compatibility of the Nb-based interlayer reduce the driving force for pure diffusion creep.
The Nb-based interlayer promotes dislocation activity as stress or temperature increases.
The changes in diffusion and dislocation activity shift the dominant creep mechanism from diffusion-mediated to dislocation-mediated creep.
Compared with otherwise identical HEA coatings without the Nb-based interlayer, the modified multilayer will exhibit a measurable shift from diffusion-controlled to dislocation-controlled creep.
The Nb-based interlayer will reduce diffusion-creep rates.
The Nb-based interlayer will cause dislocation-mediated deformation to begin at lower applied stresses than in the baseline coating.
The proposed effect requires the Nb-based interlayer to maintain coherent interfaces.
The proposed effect requires the diffusivity of the Nb-based interlayer to remain within a moderate range.
Extreme temperature or stress conditions can override the interlayer-mediated creep transition.
The quantitative magnitude of the creep-mechanism transition remains undetermined.
The performance of the Nb-based interlayer under combined high-temperature and irradiation conditions remains undetermined.
